title.en: Man killed by 13ft great white shark in Western Australia
title.zh: 西澳大利亚州一男子遭13英尺大白鲨袭击身亡

summary.en: The man was bitten just before 10:00 (03:00 BST) at Horseshoe Reef - north-west of the popular Rottnest Island near the city of Perth, local police said.
summary.zh: 当地警方表示，该男子在珀斯市附近热门的罗特内斯特岛西北部的马蹄礁，于上午10点（英国夏令时凌晨3点）前遭到袭击。

body.en:
A 38-year-old man has been killed by a 13ft (4m) great white shark in Western Australia.

On Saturday, the man was bitten just before 10:00 (03:00 BST) at Horseshoe Reef - north-west of the popular Rottnest Island near the city of Perth, local police said.

Aerial footage showed the man being rushed to shore by boat where paramedics and police performed CPR at the Geordie Bay jetty, local media ABC reported.

The state's Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development told AFP news agency it received a report the man was bitten by the great white.

The department urged the public to take "additional caution" in waters around the area.

The attack is the first fatal incident in Western Australia since March last year, when a surfer was mauled off a remote beach.

Since records began in 1791, there have been almost 1,300 recorded shark attacks in Australia, with more than 260 of them resulting in death.

Earlier this year in January, four shark attacks were reported along the New South Wales coast over two days.

One of the victims included 12-year-old Nico Antic who jumped from a rock into the Sydney Harbour and was attacked by a suspected bull shark.

He died a week later, with his parents saying in a joint statement they were "heartbroken".
body.zh: 一名 38 岁男子在西澳大利亚被一条 13 英尺（4m）长的大白鲨杀死。 当地警方称，周六 10:00（英国夏令时 03:00）前，该男子在马蹄礁 (Horseshoe Reef) 被咬，马蹄礁位于珀斯市附近热门的罗特尼斯岛 (Rottnest Island) 西北部。 据当地媒体美国广播公司报道，航拍画面显示，这名男子被乘船紧急送往岸边，医护人员和警察在乔迪湾码头进行了心肺复苏术。 该州第一产业和区域发展部告诉法新社，他们收到报告称该男子被大白鲨咬伤。 该部门敦促公众在该地区周围水域“格外小心”。 这次袭击是自去年三月以来西澳大利亚州发生的第一起致命事件，当时一名冲浪者在偏远的海滩上被殴打。 自 1791 年有记录以来，澳大利亚已记录近 1,300 起鲨鱼袭击事件，其中 260 多起导致死亡。 今年一月初，新南威尔士州海岸两天内发生了四起鲨鱼袭击事件。 其中一名受害者包括12岁的尼科·安蒂克(Nico Antic)，他从岩石上跳入悉尼港，遭到疑似牛鲨的袭击。 一周后他去世了，他的父母在一份联合声明中表示，他们“心碎”。

reflection.en: This tragic incident is a stark reminder of life's fragility and the unpredictable nature of our world. It underscores the universal truth that for each person, there is an appointed time to die. Such moments call us to reflect on the preciousness of every day and the ultimate reality we all face.
reflection.zh: 这起悲剧事件提醒我们生命的脆弱和世界的不可预测性。它强调了一个普遍的真理，即每个人都有一个注定的死亡时刻。这样的时刻促使我们反思每一天的宝贵以及我们都将面对的最终现实。

verse.textEn: Just as people are destined to die once, and after that to face judgment.
verse.textZh: 按着定命，人人都有一死，死后且有审判。

title.en: ‘Why are we even doing this?’ The week that left Britain’s PM looking like an interim leader
title.zh: “我们为什么要这样做？”英国首相看起来像“临时领导人”的一周

summary.en: A week of intense leadership jostling has left Britain's Prime Minister, Keir Starmer, appearing vulnerable and short on time, even as no official challenger has emerged. The political uncertainty was highlighted during a BBC interview where questions arose about potential moves to remove him.
summary.zh: 经过一周激烈的领导层争夺，英国首相基尔·斯塔默显得脆弱且时间紧迫，尽管尚未有正式挑战者浮出水面。在一次BBC采访中，当被问及罢免他的潜在举动时，这种政治不确定性被凸显出来。

body.en: Week of leadership jostling has left Keir Starmer looking vulnerable and short of time – even though no challenger has officially come forward It was a minute or so into his BBC interview on Friday morning, after being asked about “moves” to remove Keir Starmer, that Steve Reed ran out of patience. “There is no contest,” he interrupted. “‘Moves’ mean nothing. People need 81 nominations to stand against the prime minister.” The housing secretary, a close ally of Starmer and a founding member of the Labour Together thinktank that catapulted him to power, was right, of course: no one has formally challenged the prime minister, let alone ousted him. Continue reading...
body.zh: 一周的领导权争夺让基尔·斯塔默显得脆弱且时间紧迫——尽管还没有正式的挑战者。周五早上接受 BBC 采访后，在被问及罢免基尔·斯塔默的“举措”后，史蒂夫·里德 (Steve Reed) 失去了耐心。 “没有竞争，”他打断道。 “‘行动’毫无意义。人们需要 81 项提名才能反对总理。”这位住房部长是斯塔默的亲密盟友，也是帮助斯塔默上台的工党智囊团的创始成员，他的观点当然是对的：没有人正式挑战总理，更不用说驱逐他了。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The political jostling described in the news highlights the importance of clear vision in leadership. When a sense of direction is lacking, or a leader's authority appears diminished, it can lead to internal unrest and a feeling that the system is adrift. This reminds us that a shared, compelling vision is crucial for stability and purpose within any...
reflection.zh: 新闻中描述的政治争斗凸显了领导层清晰愿景的重要性。当方向感缺失，或领导者的权威似乎减弱时，可能会导致内部动荡和一种随波逐流的感觉。这提醒我们，一个共同的、引人注目的愿景对于任何社区或国家的稳定和目标都至关重要。

verse.textEn: Where there is no revelation, people cast off restraint; but blessed is the one who heeds wisdom's instruction.
verse.textZh: 没有异象，民就放肆；惟遵守律法的，便为有福。

title.en: Trump says senior IS leader killed by US and Nigerian forces
title.zh: 特朗普称美国和尼日利亚军队击毙高级IS头目

summary.en: The US president announced that a joint operation by US and Nigerian forces successfully killed Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, described as "the most active terrorist in the world."
summary.zh: 美国总统宣布，美国和尼日利亚军队联合行动，成功击毙了被其称为“世界上最活跃的恐怖分子”的阿布-比拉勒·米努基。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump says that American and Nigerian forces have killed the "second in command of ISIS globally" in a military operation in Africa.

Writing on Truth Social, Trump said the joint mission was "flawlessly executed... to eliminate the most active terrorist in the world", Abu-Bilal al-Minuki.

Al‑Minuki was declared a Specially Designated Global Terrorist by Washington in 2023.

The Nigerian military has not yet commented on the raid. If confirmed, his killing could mark another significant setback for Islamic State group (IS) following the killing of its leader Abu Bakr al‑Baghdadi in 2019.

Al-Minuki, also known as Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al‑Mainuki, directed IS‑linked cells across Africa, particularly the Islamic State West Africa Province, which has entrenched itself in the Lake Chad Basin and Sahel, with cross‑border links into Niger, Chad, and Mali.

Trump's message did not provide further details of the operation or the timeline of the joint mission.

Trump describes his death as a major blow to IS's African and global networks, disrupting funding channels and command structures.

The US president thanked the Nigerian government for their "partnership", adding that Minuki "will no longer terrorize the people of Africa or help plan operations to target Americans".

Nigeria and the US have increased military cooperation as the country ramps up efforts to fight extremist violence.

In April, IS claimed responsibility after gunmen killed at least 29 people at a football pitch in Nigeria's north-eastern Adamawa state.

Last Christmas, US and Nigeria carried out a joint airstrike in Nigeria's Sokoto state targeting IS-linked groups.
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，美国和尼日利亚军队在非洲的一次军事行动中击毙了“伊斯兰国全球二号人物”。 特朗普在《Truth Social》上撰文称，联合任务“完美执行……旨在消灭世界上最活跃的恐怖分子”阿布-比拉尔·米努基。 2023 年，阿尔米努基被华盛顿列为特别指定的全球恐怖分子。 尼日利亚军方尚未对此次袭击发表评论。如果得到证实，他的被杀可能标志着伊斯兰国组织 (IS) 继 2019 年杀害其领导人阿布·巴克尔·巴格达迪 (Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi) 后的又一次重大挫折。 米努基，又名阿布·伯克尔·本·穆罕默德·本·阿里·迈努基，指挥着整个非洲与伊斯兰国有关联的组织，特别是伊斯兰国西非省，该省在乍得湖盆地和萨赫勒地区根深蒂固，与尼日尔、乍得和马里有跨境联系。 特朗普的信息没有提供行动的进一步细节或联合任务的时间表。 特朗普称他的死是对伊斯兰国非洲和全球网络的重大打击，扰乱了资金渠道和指挥结构。 美国总统感谢尼日利亚政府的“合作伙伴”，并补充说米努基“将不再恐吓非洲人民或帮助计划针对美国人的行动”。 随着尼日利亚加大力度打击极端主义暴力，尼日利亚和美国加强了军事合作。 今年 4 月，枪手在尼日利亚东北部阿达马瓦州的一个足球场杀害了至少 29 人，IS 声称对此负责。 去年圣诞节，美国和尼日利亚对尼日利亚索科托州进行了联合空袭，目标是与伊斯兰国有关的组织。

reflection.en: News of a terrorist leader's elimination reminds us that the struggle against evil often involves confronting its human agents. Yet, Scripture teaches us that our ultimate battle is not merely against individuals, but against the spiritual forces that fuel such darkness. This perspective calls us to pray for wisdom and discernment in addressing the roots of...
reflection.zh: 恐怖分子头目被清除的消息提醒我们，与邪恶的斗争常常涉及对抗其人类代理人。然而，圣经教导我们，我们最终的争战不仅仅是与个人对抗，更是与助长这种黑暗的属灵势力对抗。这一视角呼吁我们为智慧和洞察力祷告，以解决仇恨和暴力的根源。

verse.textEn: For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms.
verse.textZh: 因我们并不是与属血气的争战，乃是与那些执政的、掌权的、管辖这幽暗世界的，以及天空属灵气的恶魔争战。

title.en: Teenager Isla Bell’s body was found in a Melbourne tip 18 months ago. Today friends and family demanded ‘justice’
title.zh: 青少年伊斯拉·贝尔的尸体于18个月前在墨尔本垃圾场被发现。今天，亲友们要求“伸张正义”

summary.en: Supporters gathered at the Victorian state library to protest the decision by prosecutors to drop a manslaughter charge against the man accused of killing 19-year-old Isla Bell, whose body was found in a Melbourne tip 18 months ago.
summary.zh: 19岁的伊斯拉·贝尔的尸体于18个月前在墨尔本的一个垃圾场被发现。她的支持者在维多利亚州立图书馆抗议检察官撤销对被控杀害她的男子的过失杀人指控。

body.en: Supporters at the Victorian state library protested against prosecutors dropping a manslaughter charge against the man accused of killing her Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Isla Bell, the 19-year-old whose body was found in a Melbourne tip 18 months ago, has been remembered as a loving, courageous and open-hearted young woman with a green thumb and an “exquisitely beautiful soul”. Friends, family and supporters gathered outside the Victorian state library on Saturday to honour the teenager and protest against prosecutors dropping a manslaughter charge against the man who had been accused of killing her. Continue reading...
body.zh: 维多利亚州州立图书馆的支持者抗议检察官撤销对被指控杀害她的男子的过失杀人指控。 19 岁的艾拉·贝尔 (Isla Bell) 的尸体于 18 个月前在墨尔本的一处小报中被发现，她被认为是一位充满爱心、勇敢、心胸开阔的年轻女性，拥有园艺天赋和“精致美丽的灵魂”。周六，朋友、家人和支持者聚集在维多利亚州立图书馆外，向这名少女致敬，并抗议检察官撤销对被指控杀害她的男子的过失杀人指控。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The anguish of Isla Bell's family and friends highlights the deep human need for justice and accountability, especially when the legal system appears to falter. Their protest echoes a lament for a world where the law can seem paralyzed, and justice struggles to prevail.
reflection.zh: 伊斯拉·贝尔的亲友们的痛苦凸显了人类对正义和问责制的深切需求，尤其当法律体系似乎出现问题时。他们的抗议呼应了对一个法律可能瘫痪、正义难以伸张的世界的哀叹。

verse.textEn: The law is paralyzed, and justice never prevails. The wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.
verse.textZh: 因此律法放松，公理也不显明；恶人围困义人，所以公理显然颠倒。

title.en: ‘An hour of abuse’: Jeremy Corbyn on Labour coups, and whether he feels sorry for Starmer
title.zh: “一小时的谩骂”：杰里米·科尔宾谈工党政变，以及他是否同情斯塔默

summary.en: Former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn reflected on his own expulsion from the party and the current slow ousting of Prime Minister Keir Starmer, expressing personal sympathy for Starmer's difficult experience.
summary.zh: 前工党领袖杰里米·科尔宾回顾了自己被开除党籍的经历，并谈到现任首相基尔·斯塔默正经历的缓慢下台过程，他表示对斯塔默的艰难处境感到个人同情。

body.en: As Keir Starmer endures a slow ousting as PM, former Labour leader Corbyn recalls his own expulsion and looks at the runners and riders “Yeah, I do feel [sorry for him],” said Jeremy Corbyn, with only a little hesitation. “On a personal level it must be devastating. It is a horrible feeling. You suddenly realise that this person doesn’t trust you at all and really doesn’t wish you well at all, and you suddenly realise that any trust that was there actually disappears.” There are few in politics who have had the experience of being the subject of a Labour party-style coup, the British equivalent of being dragged from your office to be put up against a wall. Letters of resignations from so-called political friends, condemnatory statements on social media, all dripped out for maximum effect with the end goal of pushing the target, once the subject of standing ovations and gushing plaudits, out on their tail. Continue reading...
body.zh: 当基尔·斯塔默（Keir Starmer）缓慢地被赶下首相职位时，前工党领袖科尔宾回忆起自己被驱逐的经历，并看着跑步者和骑手，“是的，我确实感到（为他感到遗憾），”杰里米·科尔宾（Jeremy Corbyn）说道，只有一点犹豫。 “就个人而言，这一定是毁灭性的。这是一种可怕的感觉。你突然意识到这个人根本不信任你，而且根本不希望你过得好，你突然意识到任何信任实际上都消失了。”政坛上很少有人有过成为工党式政变对象的经历，这在英国相当于被从办公室拖到墙上。所谓政治朋友的辞职信、社交媒体上的谴责声明，所有这些都是为了达到最大效果，最终目标是将曾经受到起立鼓掌和热烈喝彩的目标推向尾随。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Political careers often involve dramatic shifts, with leaders experiencing both elevation and downfall. This story reminds us of the personal cost when power dynamics change, and how quickly fortunes can turn. Psalm 75:7 offers a perspective that beyond human machinations, it is 雅伟 who ultimately determines who rises and falls.
reflection.zh: 政治生涯常伴随着戏剧性的起伏，领导者经历着被推举和被罢黜。这个故事提醒我们，当权力格局改变时，个人所付出的代价，以及命运如何迅速逆转。诗篇75:7提供了一个视角，即超越人类的谋划，最终是雅伟决定谁升谁降。

verse.textEn: It is God who judges: He brings one down, he exalts another.
verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

title.en: UK drivers struggle to get insurance for Chinese EVs such as Jaecoo
title.zh: 英国司机难以获得中国电动汽车如捷途的保险

summary.en: Research indicates that UK insurers are more reluctant to provide coverage for some Chinese hybrid and electric vehicles (EVs) or charge higher premiums compared to similar petrol cars. This trend suggests a disparity in how these vehicles are assessed in the insurance market.
summary.zh: 研究显示，英国保险公司对部分中国产混合动力和电动汽车（EV）的承保意愿低于其他国家的汽车，或者收取更高的保费。这一趋势表明，这些车辆在保险市场上面临着不同的评估标准。

body.en: Firms do not offer cover for some models, or charge more than for equivalent petrol cars, research finds UK insurers are more hesitant to cover some hybrid and electric vehicles (EVs) from China than cars from other countries, research suggests. While some drivers can save money by buying cars made in China, they may have more limited options to get insurance than those buying electric, hybrid and petrol cars from Europe, the US and South Korea. Continue reading...
body.zh: 研究发现，与其他国家的汽车相比，英国保险公司对中国的一些混合动力和电动汽车（EV）承保更加犹豫。虽然一些司机可以通过购买中国制造的汽车来省钱，但与购买欧洲、美国和韩国的电动、混合动力和汽油汽车的人相比，他们获得保险的选择可能更加有限。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The challenges faced by drivers of Chinese EVs in securing fair insurance highlight the complexities of market dynamics and perceived value. In commerce, the principle of honest measures reminds us to seek fairness and transparency in all dealings, ensuring that all are treated equitably.
reflection.zh: 中国电动汽车车主在获得公平保险方面遇到的挑战，凸显了市场动态和感知价值的复杂性。在商业中，诚实度量的原则提醒我们要在所有交易中寻求公平和透明，确保每个人都受到公正的对待。

verse.textEn: Do not use dishonest standards when measuring length, weight or quantity. Use honest scales and honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin.
verse.textZh: 你们施行审判，不可行不义；在尺、秤、升、斗上也是如此。要用公道天平、公道法码、公道升斗、公道秤。

title.en: Record numbers of UK renters crowdfunding to cover bills
title.zh: 英国租房者通过众筹支付账单的人数创历史新高

summary.en: A record number of people in the UK are resorting to crowdfunding platforms like GoFundMe to cover their rent and household bills. Rent-related fundraisers have increased by 60% since 2022, with 100,000 donors contributing to help individuals maintain their housing.
summary.zh: 英国通过众筹平台（如GoFundMe）支付租金和家庭账单的人数创历史新高。自2022年以来，与租金相关的筹款活动增加了60%，有10万名捐助者帮助人们维持住房。

body.en: Rent donations on GoFundMe up 60% since 2022, with 100,000 donors helping people keep a roof over their heads A record number of people in the UK are turning to crowdfunding to cover rent and household bills, with GoFundMe reporting more rent-related fundraisers were created in April than in any month on record. The platform said donations towards rent support had risen by 60% since 2022, with more than 100,000 people a month contributing to help others meet their housing costs. Continue reading...
body.zh: 自 2022 年以来，GoFundMe 上的租金捐赠增加了 60%，有 100,000 名捐赠者帮助人们维持生计。英国通过众筹来支付租金和家庭账单的人数创历史新高，GoFundMe 报告称，4 月份与租金相关的筹款活动比有记录以来任何一个月都要多。该平台表示，自 2022 年以来，用于租金支持的捐款增加了 60%，每月有超过 10 万人捐款帮助他人支付住房费用。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The increasing reliance on crowdfunding for basic needs highlights the growing financial strain many households face. This collective effort to help neighbors keep a roof over their heads echoes a timeless call to share resources and provide shelter for those in need. It reminds us of the profound impact of practical compassion in times of hardship.
reflection.zh: 越来越多的人依赖众筹来满足基本需求，这凸显了许多家庭日益增长的经济压力。这种帮助邻居维持住房的集体努力，呼应了分享资源、为有需要者提供住所的永恒呼召。它提醒我们在困难时期，实际的怜悯能产生深远的影响。

verse.textEn: Is it not to share your food with the hungry and to provide the poor wanderer with shelter — when you see the naked, to clothe them?
verse.textZh: 不是要把你的饼分给饥饿的人，将飘流的穷人接到你家中，见赤身的给他衣服遮体？

title.en: Trump warns Taiwan against declaring independence, hours after summit with China's Xi
title.zh: 特朗普警告台湾不要宣布独立，此前数小时曾与中国国家主席习近平举行峰会

summary.en: Following a summit with China's Xi, the US president issued a warning to Taiwan against declaring independence, urging both Beijing and Taipei to de-escalate tensions over the self-governing island.
summary.zh: 在与中国国家主席习近平举行峰会后，美国总统警告台湾不要宣布独立，并敦促北京和台北双方缓和围绕这个自治岛屿的紧张局势。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has cautioned Taiwan against formally declaring independence from China.

"I'm not looking to have somebody go independent," the US president told Fox News on Friday, at the end of his two-day summit with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Beijing.

Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te has previously stated that Taiwan does not need to declare formal independence because it already sees itself as a sovereign nation.

The US has long supported Taiwan, including being bound by law to provide it with a means of self-defence, but has frequently had to square this alliance with maintaining a diplomatic relationship with China.

Trump earlier said he had "made no commitment either way" about the self-governing island - which China claims as part of its territory and has not ruled out taking by force.

Washington's established position is that it does not support Taiwanese independence, with continued ties with Beijing being contingent on its acceptance that there is only one Chinese government.

Beijing has been vocal in its dislike of Taiwan's president, who it has previously described as a "troublemaker" and a "destroyer of cross-strait peace".

Many Taiwanese consider themselves to be part of a separate nation - though most are in favour of maintaining the status quo in which Taiwan neither declares independence from China nor unites with it.

In his interview with Fox News, Trump reiterated that US policy on the matter had not changed.

"You know, we're supposed to travel 9,500 miles (15,289km) to fight a war. I'm not looking for that. I want them to cool down. I want China to cool down."

On the flight back to Washington, the US president had told reporters that he and Xi had spoken "a lot" about the island, but said he had declined to discuss whether the US would defend it.

Xi "feels very strongly" about the island and "doesn't want to see a movement for independence", Trump said.

"The Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations," Xi warned during the talks, according to Chinese state media, adding: "If mishandled, the two nations could collide or even come into conflict."

Asked if he foresaw a conflict with China over Taiwan, Trump had said: "No, I don't think so. I think we'll be fine. [Xi] doesn't want to see a war."

China has ramped up military drills around the island in recent years, raising tensions in the region and testing the balance that Washington has struck.

Late last year, the Trump administration announced an $11bn ($8bn) package of weapons to be sold to Taiwan , including advanced rocket launchers and a variety of missiles, which Beijing condemned.

Trump said he would soon decide whether that sale could go ahead, adding that he and Xi had discussed it "in great detail".

title.en: New outbreak of Ebola kills 80 in eastern DR Congo
title.zh: 刚果民主共和国东部埃博拉疫情新爆发，已致80人死亡

summary.en: A new outbreak of Ebola has killed 80 people in eastern DR Congo, with approximately 246 cases reported by Africa's top health agency. A case has also been confirmed in neighboring Uganda.
summary.zh: 非洲最高卫生机构表示，刚果民主共和国东部爆发的新一轮埃博拉疫情已导致80人死亡，约有246例病例报告。邻国乌干达也报告了一例病例。

body.en:
Africa's top health agency has declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo's eastern Ituri province.

Around 246 cases and 80 deaths have been reported, mainly in the gold-mining towns of Mongwalu and Rwampara, said the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC).

Ugandan officials confirmed one case of imported Ebola from DR Congo on Friday, with the country's health ministry stating that a 59-year-old male who died on Thursday had tested positive.

Ebola was first discovered in 1976 in what is now DR Congo, and is thought to have spread from bats. This is the 17th outbreak of the deadly viral disease in the country.

It is spread through direct contact with bodily fluids and through broken skin, causing severe bleeding and organ failure.

Early symptoms include fever, muscle pain, fatigue, headache and sore throat, and are followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, a rash and bleeding.

There is no proven cure for Ebola. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), the average fatality rate is around 50%.

Preliminary tests conducted at the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale (INRB) in the capital, Kinshasa, have detected the virus in 13 of 20 samples analysed, following consultations with DR Congo's Ministry of Health and National Public Institute.

Of the 80 deaths, four were reported among lab-confirmed cases, Africa CDC said.

Additional suspected cases have also been reported in Ituri's provincial capital, Bunia, with laboratory confirmation pending.

Africa CDC said it was concerned by the high risk of further spread due to the urban settings of Rwampara and Bunia, and mining activities in Mongwalu.

The health agency's executive director Dr Jean Kaseya added that "significant population movement" between the affected areas and neighbouring countries also meant regional co-ordination was essential.

All affected communities and at-risk areas have been advised to follow guidelines from the national health authorities.

The Congolese government has not yet officially declared an outbreak. A staffer told the BBC a press conference was expected later on Friday.

Its statement on Friday added that it was convening a meeting with DR Congo, neighbouring Uganda and South Sudan, and other international partners to discuss priorities, including response efforts and cross-border surveillance.

Ituri has been under military rule since 2021, with the civilian authority replaced by a military general in an attempt to neutralise dozens of armed groups which have operated in the area for many years. These include the Allied Democratic Forced (ADF), affiliated to the Islamic State group.

body.zh: 非洲最高卫生机构宣布刚果民主共和国东部伊图里省爆发埃博拉疫情。 非洲疾病控制和预防中心 (Africa CDC) 表示，已报告约 246 例病例和 80 人死亡，主要发生在金矿城镇蒙瓦卢 (Mongwalu) 和鲁万帕拉 (Rwampara)。 乌干达官员周五确认了一例从刚果民主共和国输入的埃博拉病例，该国卫生部表示，周四死亡的一名 59 岁男性检测结果呈阳性。 埃博拉病毒于 1976 年在现在的刚果民主共和国首次发现，被认为是通过蝙蝠传播的。这是该国第 17 次爆发致命病毒性疾病。 它通过直接接触体液和破损的皮肤传播，导致严重出血和器官衰竭。 早期症状包括发烧、肌肉疼痛、疲劳、头痛和喉咙痛，随后出现呕吐、腹泻、皮疹和出血。 埃博拉病毒尚无有效治疗方法。根据世界卫生组织 (WHO) 的数据，平均死亡率约为 50%。 在与刚果民主共和国卫生部和国家公共研究所协商后，首都金沙萨国家生物医学研究所 (INRB) 进行的初步测试已在分析的 20 个样本中的 13 个样本中检测到了该病毒。 非洲疾病预防控制中心表示，在 80 例死亡中，有 4 例是实验室确诊病例。 伊图里省首府布尼亚还报告了更多疑似病例，有待实验室确认。 非洲疾病预防控制中心表示，由于鲁万帕拉和布尼亚的城市环境以及蒙瓦鲁的采矿活动，该病毒进一步传播的高风险感到担忧。 该卫生机构执行主任让·卡塞亚博士补充说，受影响地区和邻国之间的“大量人口流动”也意味着区域协调至关重要。 建议所有受影响的社区和高危地区遵循国家卫生当局的指导方针。 刚果政府尚未正式宣布疫情爆发。一名工作人员告诉英国广播公司，预计周五晚些时候将举行新闻发布会。 该组织周五的声明补充说，它正在与刚果民主共和国、邻国乌干达和南苏丹以及其他国际伙伴召开会议，讨论优先事项，包括应对工作和跨境监视。 伊图里自 2021 年以来一直处于军事统治之下，文职当局被一名军事将领取代，试图消灭在该地区活动多年的数十个武装团体。其中包括附属于伊斯兰国组织的民主同盟军（ADF）。 根据分享的一封信，周五，乌干达卫生部门确认发现了一例输入性埃博拉病例。

reflection.en: An Ebola outbreak in DR Congo reminds us of life's fragility and the widespread suffering disease can bring. In such times, the biblical call to pray for the sick offers a profound response, inviting us to bring those afflicted before God. This encourages both spiritual support and practical compassion for communities facing such a severe health crisis.
reflection.zh: 刚果民主共和国爆发的埃博拉疫情提醒我们生命的脆弱以及疾病可能带来的广泛痛苦。在这样的时刻，圣经呼吁为病人祷告，提供了一个深刻的回应，邀请我们将受苦的人带到雅伟面前。这鼓励我们为面临如此严重健康危机的社区提供精神支持和实际的关怀。

verse.textEn: Is anyone among you sick? Let them call the elders of the church to pray over them.
verse.textZh: 你们中间有病了的呢，他就该请教会的长老来；他们可以奉主的名用油抹他，为他祷告。

title.en: Judge declares another mistrial in Harvey Weinstein New York rape case
title.zh: 法官宣布哈维·韦恩斯坦纽约强奸案再次审判流产

summary.en: A New York judge has declared another mistrial in the rape case against former film mogul Harvey Weinstein. This marks the third time a jury has considered the charges against the 74-year-old.
summary.zh: 纽约一名法官宣布，针对前电影大亨哈维·韦恩斯坦的强奸案再次审判流产。这是纽约陪审团第三次审理这名74岁声名狼藉的电影大亨的案件。

body.en:
A judge has declared a mistrial in the rape case against Harvey Weinstein, after the jury in New York said it was deadlocked and unable to reach a verdict.

It marks the third time a New York jury has considered the case against the 74-year-old disgraced film mogul, who remains jailed on other charges.

The month-long trial was centred around whether Weinstein raped aspiring actress Jessica Mann more than a decade ago. He was initially convicted, but the verdict was overturned. A judge declared a mistrial after a second trial last year.

Dozens of women have accused Weinstein of sexual misconduct, including rape, since October 2017. He has consistently denied wrongdoing.

Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg said in a statement that prosecutors are currently determining whether to try again in court.

"While we are disappointed that the proceedings ended with a mistrial, we deeply respect the jury system and sincerely thank all of the jurors for their time and dedication," he said.

He thanked Mann for bringing her allegation against Weinstein, adding: "We will consider our next steps in consultation with Ms Mann, and in consideration of Harvey Weinstein's pending sentencing" in a separate sexual assault case.

"As always, we will continue to prosecute crimes of sexual violence – no matter who the defendant is – in a survivor-centered manner that uplifts their voices in the pursuit of justice."

Lawyers for Weinstein said the outcome shows "how deeply public perception and prejudice surrounding Harvey Weinstein have become embedded in society".

"For some people, regardless of the evidence presented, saying 'not guilty' has become emotionally or socially impossible," they argued.

"The Manhattan District Attorney's Office should stop retrying the same case and focus its time and resources on the actual violent crime, chaos, and public safety issues impacting New Yorkers every day," the statement from his lawyers continued.

The decision on Friday by the majority male jury in Manhattan came on the third day of deliberations.

On Friday morning, the jury passed the judge a note saying they "have concluded that they cannot reach" a unanimous verdict. The judge then ordered them to continue deliberating before later declaring a mistrial, saying it was "quite clear", that they were "hopelessly deadlocked".

"I see no reason to go any further," said Judge Curtis Farber as he thanked and dismissed the jury.

Weinstein, who was seated in a wheelchair during the trial, showed no reaction as court officers wheeled him out of the room after the mistrial was declared.

Speaking to reporters outside the court, one juror said that nine people on the jury wanted to acquit Weinstein, while three wanted to convict him, according to the Associated Press.

title.en: Hopes for 'lasting peace': Israel and Lebanon extend ceasefire by 45-days
title.zh: 以色列和黎巴嫩停火延长45天，有望实现“持久和平”

summary.en: A US official has described the talks between the countries as "highly productive".
summary.zh: 一位美国官员形容两国之间的会谈“富有成效”。

body.en:
Israel and Lebanon agreed to a 45-day extension of a ceasefire that has tamped down the conflict between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah in southern Lebanon , as two days of talks facilitated by the US concluded.

"The April 16 cessation of hostilities will be extended by 45 days to enable further progress," State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott wrote on X.

Pigott added that the talks aimed at settling decades of conflict between the two countries were "highly productive."

The Lebanese and Israeli delegations issued positive statements about the talks, their third meeting since Israel intensified air attacks on Lebanon after Hezbollah fired missiles at Israel on 2 March, three days into the US-Israeli war with Iran.

Israel's bombing campaign and ground invasion of Lebanon's south displaced about 1.2 million people, before US President Donald Trump announced a ceasefire last month following initial talks between the two countries' ambassadors in the US.

Hezbollah and Israel have ongoing clashes, mainly in southern Lebanon, where Israeli forces are occupying a self-declared security zone.

The US-led mediation between Lebanon and Israel has emerged in parallel to diplomacy aimed at ending the US-Iran conflict. Iran has ⁠said ending Israel's war in Lebanon is one of its demands for a deal over the wider conflict.

Lebanon's delegation, which is attending despite objections from Hezbollah, has prioritised a cessation in hostilities in the talks. Israel says Hezbollah must be disarmed as part of any broader peace agreement with Lebanon.

The Washington D.C. meetings, the highest-level contact between Lebanon and Israel in decades, have evolved to include security and military officials.

Pigott said on X that a new "security track" of the negotiations would be launched at the Pentagon on 29 May, while the US State Department will convene the two sides again at the start of June for a political track of negotiations.

"We hope these discussions will advance lasting peace between the two countries, full recognition of each other’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and establishing genuine security along their shared border," Pigott said.

Lebanon's delegation said in a statement that it wanted to turn the momentum from the ceasefire into a lasting peace agreement.

"The extension of the ceasefire and the establishment of a U.S.-facilitated security track provide critical breathing space for our citizens, reinforce state institutions, and advance a political pathway toward lasting stability," the delegation said.

Israeli ambassador to the US, Yechiel Leiter, also described the talks as "frank and constructive."

"There will be ups and downs, but the potential for success is great. What will be paramount throughout negotiations...

title.en: In the Eurovision press room, Delta Goodrem passed the vibe check
title.zh: 在欧洲歌唱大赛新闻发布会上，黛尔塔·古德伦通过了氛围测试

summary.en: Finland remains a finals favourite, but Delta has serious momentum. Could it be enough to carry her to a win?
summary.zh: 芬兰仍然是决赛热门，但黛尔塔势头强劲。这股势头能否助她赢得胜利？

body.en:
Reporting on Eurovision is an odd experience. You don’t sit in the arena itself; organisers aren’t keen to hand free seats to journalists when they can be sold for hundreds of Euros each.

Instead, you sit in a nearby press centre, watching the broadcast on a big screen. Unlike most press centres, people dress up, dance along to the songs they like and cheer as if they were in the front row.

Often, it’s a useful barometer to judge how an act is going to go. These people know their Eurovision.

For most of the week, Delta had been fourth or fifth most likely to win according to bookies. After her semi-final, she rocketed up to second.

Over the last decade, the bookies do normally get it right. Last year was an exception, Austria’s operatic JJ took the title with Wasted Love , despite Sweden’s jaunty ditty about the joy of Saunas, Bara Bada Bastu being the clear favourite beforehand.

“It’s a nice feeling, we’ve still got a mission to go,” she said after qualifying for the final.

In the event of an Australian win, she wants to host next year’s competition at the Rooty Hill RSL.

“Of all the performances that I have seen on this stage there has only been one that came with a level of effortless, professionalism, joy, hair flicks, piano playing and elevation into the sky,” she tells me.

Danny Estrin, lead singer of Voyager (Australia, 2023) and now Courtney’s co-commentator, thinks that ‘effortlessness’ is a result of experience and preparation.

“By the time you get to performing it, having rehearsed it, it becomes second nature to you,” he explains.

“If you approach it with an element of fun, it translates. She had a cheeky smile, like ‘this is what I do every single day.’

But so, it seems, will the UK’s legendary commentator Graham Norton, who has not always been a fan of Australia’s involvement in the contest.

“Australia have kind of knocked it out of the park this year,” he told the BBC.

“It is just brilliant. I know it's pathetic, but I was gasping. It was so good. So I think they might be the ones to beat now."

This is my eighth Eurovision Song Contest (if you include the one I went to as a backpacker in Dusseldorf with a ticket bought from a scalper.)

My track record of predicting the winner is not bad; if you tip the favourite, you generally end up being right.

Finland’s Liekinheitin has all the ingredients of a Eurovision winner, yet it just doesn’t feel like a Eurovision winner to me.

body.zh: 报道欧洲电视网是一种奇怪的经历。你不是坐在竞技场里，而是坐在竞技场里。当记者的免费座位可以卖到数百欧元时，组织者并不热衷于向记者提供免费座位。 相反，你坐在附近的新闻中心，在大屏幕上观看广播。与大多数新闻中心不同的是，人们盛装打扮，随着自己喜欢的歌曲跳舞并欢呼，就像坐在前排一样。 通常，它是判断行为进展情况的有用晴雨表。这些人了解他们的欧洲歌唱大赛。 据博彩公司称，在本周的大部分时间里，达美航空在获胜的可能性中排名第四或第五。半决赛后，她飙升至第二位。 在过去的十年里，博彩公司通常都会做对的。去年是个例外，奥地利的歌剧 JJ 凭借《浪费的爱》夺得了冠军，尽管瑞典的欢快小曲讲述了桑拿的乐趣，《巴拉巴达巴斯图》显然是之前最受欢迎的。 “这种感觉很好，我们还有任务要做，”她在晋级决赛后说道。 如果澳大利亚队获胜，她希望在 Rooty Hill RSL 举办明年的比赛。 “在我在这个舞台上看过的所有表演中，只有一场是毫不费力、专业、欢乐、头发轻拂、钢琴演奏和升空的，”她告诉我。 《Voyager》（澳大利亚，2023 年）的主唱、现任考特尼的共同解说员丹尼·埃斯特林 (Danny Estrin) 认为，“轻松”是经验和准备的结果。 “当你开始表演、排练之后，它就会成为你的第二天性，”他解释道。 “如果你带着一种有趣的元素来对待它，它就会转化。她脸上挂着厚颜无耻的微笑，就像‘这就是我每天都会做的事情’。” 但英国传奇评论员格雷厄姆·诺顿似乎也会如此，他并不总是支持澳大利亚参与这场比赛。 “澳大利亚今年已经成功了，”他告诉英国广播公司。 “这真是太棒了。我知道这很可悲，但我却喘不过气来。真是太好了。所以我认为他们现在可能是要击败的人。” 这是我的第八届欧洲歌唱大赛（如果你把我作为背包客在杜塞尔多夫用从黄牛那里买的票去参加的比赛算在内。） 我预测获胜者的记录还不错；如果你给最喜欢的人小费，那么你通常都是对的。 芬兰的 Liekinheitin 拥有欧洲歌唱大赛冠军的所有要素，但对我来说，它感觉不像欧洲歌唱大赛的冠军。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.zh: 在竞技表演的世界里，像黛尔塔·古德伦这样的艺人以极大的自律去争取梦寐以求的奖项。这种对卓越和认可的追求，反映了运动员在争取那会朽坏的冠冕时所展现的奉献精神。然而，这节经文也提醒我们思考那不能朽坏的冠冕，鼓励我们将努力投入到真正持久、超越短暂名声的事物上。

title.en: As Xi sets a new power dynamic, Trump leaves China with little to brag about
title.zh: 习近平确立新权力格局，特朗普对中国无甚可夸

summary.en: During a largely cordial summit, signals emerged indicating a potential shift in the balance of power between the two leaders.
summary.zh: 在一场大致友好的峰会期间，有迹象表明两位领导人之间的权力平衡可能正在发生转变。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump hailed it as “the biggest summit ever.” In reality, his less than 48 lavish hours in China yielded few results.

Expectations for any real breakthroughs were always low. But what we saw at the high-stakes summit could still shape the US-China relationship for months and years to come.

China had been signalling for weeks that Taiwan would be its top priority at this summit.

The island’s status has always been a point of conflict between the US and Chinese governments; China claims it as a self-governing province that will eventually be brought under its control, while the US has long been its single largest supplier of the weapons needed to prevent that from happening.

But this week, Chinese President Xi Jinping took it one step further; saying explicitly that from now on, the most important factor in the US-China relationship would be how the US deals with Taiwan.

“The Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations,” Xi told Trump, according to the Chinese Foreign Ministry handout. “If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability. If handled poorly, the two countries will collide or even clash, putting the entire US-China relationship in an extremely dangerous situation.”

When asked for his version of events later in the day, Trump opted to say nothing. His silence was seen as a win in Taiwan, where fears he might go off script and say something to inadvertently shift the US’ position on the island were high going into the summit.

“US policy on the issue of Taiwan is unchanged as of today and as of the meeting that we had here today,” US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said. “It was raised. They always raised it on their side. We always make clear our position and we move on to other topics.”

But China has made its position clear; the US’ ongoing support for Taiwan could jeopardise one of its most important trade relationships.

The US approved a US$15b ($2.09b) arms package for Taiwan in December last year; its largest ever. But with Trump still yet to give his final approval, its delivery had been stalled.

Whether or not those weapons finally reach Taiwan may be the first real test of whether Xi’s threat made an impact.

While the summit was largely cordial, there were moments that signalled the balance of power between the two leaders might be shifting.

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普称赞这是“有史以来规模最大的峰会”。事实上，他在中国度过的不到48个小时的奢华时光并没有取得什么成果。 对任何真正突破的期望总是很低。但我们在这次高风险峰会上看到的情况仍可能影响未来数月乃至数年的美中关系。 几周来，中国一直在暗示台湾将是此次峰会的首要任务。 该岛的地位一直是美国和中国政府之间的冲突点。中国声称它是一个自治省，最终将受到其控制，而美国长期以来一直是其最大的武器供应商，以防止这种情况发生。 但本周，中国国家主席习近平更进一步；明确表示，今后美中关系最重要的因素将是美国如何对待台湾。 根据中国外交部的讲义，习近平对特朗普说：“台湾问题是中美关系中最重要的问题。” “如果处理得当，双边关系将保持总体稳定。如果处理不好，两国就会发生冲突甚至冲突，使整个美中关系处于极其危险的境地。” 当天晚些时候，当被问及他对事件的看法时，特朗普选择什么也不说。他的沉默在台湾被视为一种胜利，在峰会上，人们非常担心他可能会脱离剧本，说出一些无意中改变美国在台湾的立场的话。 美国国务卿卢比奥表示：“截至今天以及我们今天在这里举行的会议，美国在台湾问题上的政策没有变化。” “有人提出了。他们总是站在自己一边提出。我们总是明确我们的立场，然后转向其他话题。” 但中方已经明确表明立场，美国对台湾的持续支持可能会危及其最重要的贸易关系之一。 去年 12 月，美国批准了一项价值 150 亿美元（2.09b 美元）的台湾军售计划；其规模有史以来最大。但由于特朗普尚未给予最终批准，其交付已陷入停滞。 这些武器最终是否到达台湾可能是习近平的威胁是否产生影响的第一个真正考验。 尽管这次峰会基本上是友好的，但有些时刻表明两位领导人之间的权力平衡可能正在发生变化。 习近平铺上红地毯，做了很多让特朗普感到受到尊重的事情；派副总统到机场迎接他，亲自陪同他游览天坛，并允许他参观高度保密的中南海大院，他和其他中共高级官员都在那里……

reflection.en: News of shifting power dynamics among world leaders reminds us that earthly authority is always in flux. Psalm 75:7 offers a profound perspective, reminding us that it is 雅伟 who ultimately determines who rises and falls. This truth invites us to look beyond temporary political tides to the enduring sovereignty of God.

title.en: Islamic feminism more widespread in Bosnia and Herzegovina
title.zh: 伊斯兰女权主义在波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那日益普及

summary.en: Many Muslim women in Bosnia and Herzegovina are advocating for increased participation in mosque activities on Fridays and a greater role in the decision-making processes of the Islamic Community, leading to gradual changes in official structures.
summary.zh: 波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那的许多穆斯林妇女正在争取在周五参加清真寺活动，并在伊斯兰社区的决策过程中发挥更大作用，这正促使官方结构发生缓慢变化。

body.en:
Many Bosnian Muslim women want to attend mosque on Fridays and to play a greater role in decision-making. Slowly the official structures of the Islamic Community are changing.

Usually, it tends to be Muslim men who go to pray on Fridays in the mosques of Bosnia and Herzegovina. As is customary in  Islam , women are not required to go to the mosque to pray on the holiest day of the week. However, more and more, devout Muslim women in the Western Balkan country want to attend the mosque, too.

In the secular state of Bosnia and Herzegovina , men and women are equal before the law. In recent decades, the state has made significant efforts to eliminate gender-based discrimination and protect women from violence. However, in certain religious communities, whether these are Muslim, Orthodox or Catholic , social and cultural norms continue to stand in the way of equality.

Since the end of the Bosnian War (1992–1995), religion has played a greater role in all of the country's communities, particularly amid Muslim Bosniaks, Orthodox Serbs and Catholic Croats. In some families, very conservative notions of gender roles prevail, according to which women are expected first and foremost to be mothers and to care for the family.

"Muslim feminists are fighting for women's rights within an Islamic framework," Bosnian sociologist Dermana Kuric from the University of Sarajevo told DW. She said that they were doing this by taking an active role in society without openly challenging misogynistic interpretations of the Quran.

She added that university educated Muslim women were consciously engaging with traditional Islamic scholarship, which has sought to confine women to a subordinate role in the family and the wider community. "Muslim feminists are concerned with gender relations based on autonomy and individual responsibility — as opposed to control or dominance," Kuric said.

Bosnian Muslim feminists are part of a broader movement that has been gaining influence in the Islamic world since the 1980s. They interpret the Quran from a female perspective and see it as a source of empowerment in their struggle for greater rights. With her translation of the groundbreaking book by Moroccan sociologist and pioneer of Islamic feminism Fatima Mernissi (1940 – 2015) "The Forgotten Queens of Islam," gender studies scholar Zilka Spahic-Siljak from the University of Sarajevo has made a significant contribution to raising awareness of the ideas of Islamic feminism in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title.en: Ukraine: Dozens of European countries sign up to special tribunal plan to prosecute Russia
title.zh: 乌克兰：数十个欧洲国家签署特别法庭计划，以起诉俄罗斯

summary.en: At talks in Moldova, more than 30 countries have said they will join a future special tribunal for Ukraine prosecuting Russia over its invasion. How the body will force Russians to stand trial is not clear.
summary.zh: 在摩尔多瓦举行的会谈中，超过30个国家表示将加入未来针对乌克兰的特别法庭，起诉俄罗斯入侵乌克兰。目前尚不清楚该机构将如何强制俄罗斯人出庭受审。

body.zh: 在摩尔多瓦举行的会谈中，30多个国家表示，他们将加入未来的乌克兰特别法庭，起诉俄罗斯的入侵。目前还不清楚该机构将如何迫使俄罗斯人接受审判。 周五，34个欧洲国家加上澳大利亚、哥斯达黎加和欧盟作为一个实体签署了一个未来的特别法庭，该法庭将寻求起诉俄罗斯在入侵乌克兰期间犯下的罪行。 该计划自 2022 年俄罗斯全面入侵后不久就开始酝酿，乌克兰总统泽连斯基去年与欧洲委员会签署了一项协议，寻求实施该计划。 欧洲委员会在一份声明中表示，欧洲委员会的 46 个成员国中的大多数批准了一项决议，为未来的法庭奠定了基础。欧洲委员会是一个总部位于法国的机构，致力于维护人权和民主，其成员数量比欧盟还多，但不要与欧洲理事会混淆。乌克兰是其成员国。 该组织秘书长阿兰·贝尔塞特表示：“俄罗斯为其侵略行为承担责任的时间很快就要到了。” “特别法庭代表正义和希望。现在需要采取行动，通过确保法庭的运作和资金来落实这一政治承诺。” 贝尔塞特说：“今天，我们正在承担责任，确保侵略不会得不到回应。”他邀请其他国家加入这一倡议。 乌克兰外交部长安德里·西比哈是周五的参与者之一，他称这次活动是“历史性的一天”。 “就像 80 年前的纽伦堡法庭一样，海牙特别法庭将从战争废墟中恢复正义，”西比哈说，他提到了二战后一些幸存的纳粹高级分子的审判。 “我们正在建立一个由三个支柱组成的问责基础设施：特别法庭、损失登记册和索赔委员会。我还要强调，问责制永远不会妥协。” 荷兰外交部长汤姆·贝伦德森表示，荷兰已同意在海牙“主持”特别法庭的“初始阶段”，海牙是其他几个国际法律机构和程序的所在地，其中最著名的是国际刑事法院。 贝伦德森说：“乌克兰的正义之路漫长且不易，但这并不能阻止我们竭尽全力帮助实现这一目标。” 批评者质疑，鉴于弗拉基米尔·普京总统的政权似乎不太可能合作或同意其制裁，这样一个法庭将如何能够起诉被指控的俄罗​​斯战犯或国家本身。 俄罗斯曾是欧洲委员会成员，但在...

This collective action echoes the biblical call for justice to flow powerfully and continuously, seeking accountability for actions that cause immense suffering....

title.en: Pakistan faces pressure over mediator role in Iran war
title.zh: 巴基斯坦因在伊朗战争中的调解角色面临压力

summary.en: Pakistan is navigating a complex geopolitical landscape as it takes on a mediator role in a major conflict, balancing relations with Washington, Tehran, Beijing, and key Gulf allies. This delicate position has drawn increased scrutiny following a recent US media report.
summary.zh: 巴基斯坦在一次重大地缘政治冲突中扮演调解角色，正努力平衡与华盛顿、德黑兰、北京以及主要海湾盟友的关系。一份近期美国媒体的报道使这一微妙立场面临更多审视。

body.en:
With Pakistan stepping in the middle of a major geopolitical conflict, Islamabad is forced to balance between Washington, Tehran, Beijing and key Gulf allies. A recent US media report places it under even more scrutiny.

Pakistan has taken on a leading role in the peace efforts between the US and Iran , hosting talks and serving as an intermediary for backchannel diplomacy between the warring parties .

For Islamabad, the stakes are high. Officials view stability in the Gulf as closely tied to the country's own economic and security interests. A broader confrontation between the US and Iran could disrupt trade routes, deepen energy pressures, inflame sectarian tensions and further destabilize Pakistan's sensitive border regions with Iran.

International prestige is also at play for the Pakistani government as they work to end a conflict affecting the entire world . But this also means a risk of reputational damage.

"Pakistan risks growing criticism if its efforts to revive US-Iran talks fail, especially after publicly taking a leading mediation role," Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow for South Asia at the Washington-based Atlantic Council, told DW. 

"With talks stalled, Pakistan's options are limited because a mediator cannot force two deeply distrustful sides to negotiate," he added.

"Pakistan is trying its best to engage both parties and views the escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran with grave concern," a senior government official involved in the negotiation process told DW. 

"We are committed to playing a constructive diplomatic role to support immediate de-escalation and a peaceful resolution in the interest of regional and global security," the official added. 

Earlier this week, a report in US media raised doubt over Pakistan's neutrality in the Iran conflict. Citing unnamed US officials, CBS News reported that Pakistan had allowed Iran to park its aircraft on Pakistani airbases , effectively shielding them from US strikes.

Pakistan's Foreign Office immediately responded by calling the report "misleading" and "speculative." In an official statement, Islamabad said the aircraft activity was linked to diplomatic and logistical arrangements connected to ongoing peace efforts and involved personnel from multiple sides.

The Foreign Office also warned that "unverified and sensationalized reporting" risked undermining sensitive diplomatic initiatives.

US Senator Lindsey Graham, an outspoken supporter of the US war in Iran, publicly criticized Pakistan following the CBS report. His remarks reflect broader concerns among some US policymakers who fear Pakistan may be appearing too accommodating toward Tehran while still seeking to preserve strategic ties with Washington.

body.zh: 随着巴基斯坦陷入重大地缘政治冲突，伊斯兰堡被迫在华盛顿、德黑兰、北京和主要海湾盟友之间保持平衡。美国媒体最近的一篇报道对其进行了更严格的审查。 巴基斯坦在美国和伊朗之间的和平努力中发挥了主导作用，主办了会谈并充当交战双方之间秘密外交的调解人。 对于伊斯兰堡来说，风险很高。官员们认为海湾地区的稳定与该国自身的经济和安全利益密切相关。美国和伊朗之间更广泛的对抗可能会扰乱贸易路线，加深能源压力，加剧宗派紧张局势，并进一步破坏巴基斯坦与伊朗敏感边境地区的稳定。 巴基斯坦政府在努力结束影响全世界的冲突时，国际声誉也发挥着重要作用。但这也意味着声誉受损的风险。 华盛顿大西洋理事会南亚高级研究员迈克尔·库格曼（Michael Kugelman）告诉德国之声：“如果巴基斯坦恢复美伊谈判的努力失败，特别是在公开发挥主导调解作用之后，巴基斯坦将面临越来越多的批评。” 他补充说：“随着谈判陷入僵局，巴基斯坦的选择受到限制，因为调解人无法迫使两个极度不信任的双方进行谈判。” 一位参与谈判进程的高级政府官员告诉德国之声：“巴基斯坦正在尽最大努力与双方接触，并对华盛顿和德黑兰之间不断升级的紧张局势表示严重关切。” 这位官员补充道：“我们致力于发挥建设性的外交作用，支持立即缓和局势并和平解决问题，以维护地区和全球安全。” 本周早些时候，美国媒体的一篇报道对巴基斯坦在伊朗冲突中的中立性提出了质疑。哥伦比亚广播公司新闻援引未透露姓名的美国官员的话说，巴基斯坦允许伊朗将其飞机停放在巴基斯坦空军基地，从而有效地保护它们免受美国的袭击。 巴基斯坦外交部立即回应称该报告“具有误导性”和“推测性”。伊斯兰堡在一份官方声明中表示，飞机活动与正在进行的和平努力相关的外交和后勤安排有关，涉及多方人员。 英国外交部还警告说，“未经证实和耸人听闻的报道”可能会破坏敏感的外交举措。 美国参议员林赛·格雷厄姆是美国对伊朗战争的直言不讳的支持者，在哥伦比亚广播公司的报道后公开批评巴基斯坦。他的言论反映了一些美国政策制定者更广泛的担忧，他们担心巴基斯坦可能对德黑兰过于宽容，同时仍寻求维持与华盛顿的战略关系。 与此同时，美国...

The Beatitudes remind us that those who work for peace are blessed, reflecting a divine calling to bridge divides even when the path is fraught with pressure.

title.en: UK politics: How Starmer survives as Farage waits in wings
title.zh: 英国政治：斯塔默如何生存，法拉奇伺机而动

summary.en: The UK political landscape is marked by significant upheaval, including high-profile resignations, a prime minister facing pressure, and the increasing prominence of populist figures. This dynamic environment highlights the ongoing shifts within the Labour party and the rise of Nigel Farage.
summary.zh: 英国政坛正经历剧烈动荡，包括多位知名人士辞职、首相面临压力以及民粹主义者崛起。这种动态环境凸显了工党内部的持续变动以及奈杰尔·法拉奇的声势渐涨。

body.en:
High profile resignations, a prime minister on the edge and populists on the up — UK politics is far from dull. DW explains what's going on in Keir Starmer's Labour party and with Nigel Farage. And what may be next.

Less than two years after winning a landslide election victory that ended 14 years of center-right Conservative party governments in the UK, Keir Starmer is hanging by a thread.

His center-left Labour party lost well over half of their local council seats in elections held across England last week, with most going to right-wing, anti-immigration party, Reform UK. Labour also performed poorly in devolved elections for the Scottish and Welsh parliaments on the same day.

Because they operate at the national level, Starmer and his fellow Members of Parliament (MPs) weren't actually up for re-election. But the loss is perceived as a damning indictment of his lack of popularity. A survey this month by British pollsters YouGov found 23% of Britons held a positive opinion of Starmer, while 69% had an unfavorable view. He is also rapidly losing support within his party.

For now, the 63-year-old is still leading the country . Starmer's 2024 win means he is entitled to hold power until the next general election, which must be called by August 2029 at the latest. Unless he resigns, which he has so far ruled out , there are limited options to oust him during a term.

One of these is if he loses a so-called Parliamentary Vote of No Confidence. This must be tabled by an MP and Starmer must lose a simple majority in the House of Commons. Given Labour hold 403 of the 650 seats, this is unlikely. A more likely scenario is that he loses the support of his party.

More than 90 Labour MPs have called for him to go in recent days, with some high profile cabinet ministers resigning their posts. But, under Labour rules, 20% of Labour MPs — 81 people — must support a single candidate to challenge the incumbent. That scenario would trigger an internal party leadership election, the winner of which would become prime minister by default.

The early favorite isn't currently an MP. Andy Burnham is the elected Labour Mayor of Greater Manchester, one of the UK's largest cities and a traditional Labour heartland. That would ordinarily rule him out of a leadership challenge but Josh Simons, MP for Makerfield in Greater Manchester, has stepped down, forcing a byelection that Burnham hopes to win if selected by the party as candidate, giving him a seat in the House of Commons.

While Burnham has been well regarded in his mayoral stint, some will see his abandoning of Manchester for the big stage as a dereliction of duty. If he does win the byelection, Burnham will return to the national stage for the first time since 2017 having served under Tony Blair's government...
body.zh: 高调辞职、首相处于边缘、民粹主义者抬头——英国政治绝非沉闷。德国之声解释了凯尔·斯塔默 (Keir Starmer) 领导的工党和奈杰尔·法拉奇 (Nigel Farage) 的情况。接下来可能会发生什么。 凯尔·斯塔默 (Keir Starmer) 在选举中取得压倒性胜利，结束了英国 14 年的中右翼保守党政府统治，不到两年，他就命悬一线。 他的中左翼工党在上周英格兰各地举行的选举中失去了超过一半的地方议会席位，其中大部分席位被右翼反移民党改革英国所夺走。工党在同一天的苏格兰和威尔士议会权力下放选举中也表现不佳。 由于斯塔默和他的国会议员同僚是在国家层面运作的，因此他们实际上并没有竞选连任。但这次失利被认为是对他缺乏人气的严厉控诉。英国民意调查机构 YouGov 本月进行的一项调查发现，23% 的英国人对斯塔默持积极态度，而 69% 的人持负面看法。他也在党内迅速失去支持。 目前，这位63岁的老人仍然处于全国领先地位。斯塔默在 2024 年获胜意味着他有权在下一次大选之前继续掌权，而下一次大选最迟必须在 2029 年 8 月之前举行。除非他辞职（到目前为止他已经排除了这种可能性），否则在任期内罢免他的选择有限。 其中之一是如果他失去所谓的议会不信任投票。该提案必须由国会议员提出，而斯塔默必须在下议院失去简单多数。鉴于工党占据 650 个席位中的 403 个，这不太可能。更有可能的情况是他失去政党的支持。 最近几天，超过 90 名工党议员呼吁他下台，一些知名内阁部长也辞职了。但是，根据工党规定，20% 的工党议员（81 人）必须支持一名候选人才能挑战现任议员。这种情况将引发党内领导人选举，选举的获胜者将默认成为总理。 早期的热门人选目前不是国会议员。安迪·伯纳姆 (Andy Burnham) 是大曼彻斯特当选的工党市长，大曼彻斯特是英国最大的城市之一，也是传统的工党中心地带。这通常会使他排除在领导层挑战之外，但大曼彻斯特梅克菲尔德议员乔什·西蒙斯(Josh Simons)已经辞职，迫使伯纳姆进行补选，如果伯纳姆被该党选为候选人，他希望能够赢得补选，从而获得下议院席位。 尽管伯纳姆在市长任期内受到了良好的评价，但有些人会认为他放弃曼彻斯特而转向大舞台是一种失职。如果伯纳姆确实赢得补选，他将自 2017 年在托尼·布莱尔政府任职以来首次重返国家舞台……

reflection.en: In the midst of political volatility, where leaders rise and fall, this verse reminds us of a deeper truth: ultimate authority rests with God. While human decisions shape events, it is 雅伟 who ultimately determines who is brought down and who is exalted, inviting us to trust in His sovereign hand even amidst uncertainty.
reflection.zh: 在政治动荡、领袖更迭之际，这节经文提醒我们一个更深层的真理：最终的权柄在于神。虽然人类的决策影响着事态发展，但最终是雅伟决定谁被贬低，谁被高举，这邀请我们在不确定中信靠祂的主权之手。

verse.textEn: It is God who judges: He brings one down, he exalts another.
verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

title.en: The 'Thucydides trap' and Taiwan: What the US' visit to China means for Australia
title.zh: “修昔底德陷阱”与台湾：美国对中国的访问对澳大利亚意味着什么

summary.en: A recent visit by US officials to China saw President Xi Jinping assert his resolve in discussions with a less prominent Donald Trump, against the backdrop of the 'Thucydides trap' theory concerning rising and established powers, and its implications for Taiwan and Australia.
summary.zh: 美国官员近期访问中国，习近平主席在与影响力减弱的唐纳德·特朗普的会谈中展现了决心。此次访问是在关于新兴大国与既有大国之间“修昔底德陷阱”理论的背景下进行的，其对台湾和澳大利亚的影响备受关注。

body.en:
As Donald Trump heaped praise on Xi Jinping during a meeting in Beijing, it was not reciprocated by the Chinese president. Instead, Xi invoked an ancient Greek concept, signalling there could be trouble ahead.

The United States president is on a three-day state visit to China — the first by an American president since his own in 2017 — where he's hoping to secure assistance from the Iranian ally over opening the Strait of Hormuz, among other objectives.

On Thursday, before their two-hour private meeting at the Great Hall of the People, Trump lavished praise on Xi, saying he is a "great leader" and that "it's an honour to be your friend".

Xi, on the other hand, implied that the US was on the way out as global hegemon while China was quickly taking its place, with a subtle warning that its rivals ought not to stop its ascendance.

"Currently, a transformation not seen in a century is accelerating across the globe, and the international situation is fluid and turbulent," he said.

"The world has come to a new crossroads. Can China and the United States overcome the Thucydides trap and create a new paradigm of major country relations?"

That concept, referencing the Greek historian's assessment of the second Peloponnesian War of 431 BC to 404 BC, posits that a rising power strikes fear into a regional leader, making war inevitable.

According to Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning, Xi told Trump that "the Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations".

"If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability. Otherwise, the two countries will have clashes and even conflicts, putting the entire relationship in great jeopardy," Xi is alleged to have said.

Such militaristic posturing is nothing new from China, according to Bethany Allen, head of China investigations and analysis at the Australian Strategic Policy Institute (ASPI).

"It's all very, very similar language to what we've seen before," she told SBS News. "China is always firm on Taiwan."

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state who is with Trump in Beijing, has said that such remarks are routine for China.

“They always raise it on their side," he told NBC News. "We always make clear our position, and we move on to the other topics.”

The conflict in the Middle East has seen US allies — including Australia — refuse to respond to requests for assistance in opening the Strait of Hormuz. The strategic waterway's closure has driven up fuel costs around the world and impacted Trump's approval ratings domestically in the US.

title.en: Trump warns Taiwan against declaring independence, hours after summit with China's Xi

summary.en: US President Trump has cautioned Taiwan against declaring independence, following a summit with China's President Xi. He urged both Beijing and Taipei to de-escalate tensions regarding the self-governing island.
summary.zh: 美国总统特朗普在与中国国家主席习近平举行峰会后，警告台湾不要宣布独立。他敦促北京和台北双方就这个自治岛屿的紧张局势“降温”。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has cautioned Taiwan against formally declaring independence from China.

"I'm not looking to have somebody go independent," the US president told Fox News on Friday, at the end of his two-day summit with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Beijing.

Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te has previously stated that Taiwan does not need to declare formal independence because it already sees itself as a sovereign nation.

The US has long supported Taiwan, including being bound by law to provide it with a means of self-defence, but has frequently had to square this alliance with maintaining a diplomatic relationship with China.

Trump earlier said he had "made no commitment either way" about the self-governing island - which China claims as part of its territory and has not ruled out taking by force.

Washington's established position is that it does not support Taiwanese independence, with continued ties with Beijing being contingent on its acceptance that there is only one Chinese government.

Beijing has been vocal in its dislike of Taiwan's president, who it has previously described as a "troublemaker" and a "destroyer of cross-strait peace".

Many Taiwanese consider themselves to be part of a separate nation - though most are in favour of maintaining the status quo in which Taiwan neither declares independence from China nor unites with it.

In his interview with Fox News, Trump reiterated that US policy on the matter had not changed.

"You know, we're supposed to travel 9,500 miles (15,289km) to fight a war. I'm not looking for that. I want them to cool down. I want China to cool down."

On the flight back to Washington, the US president had told reporters that he and Xi had spoken "a lot" about the island, but said he had declined to discuss whether the US would defend it.

Xi "feels very strongly" about the island and "doesn't want to see a movement for independence", Trump said.

"The Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations," Xi warned during the talks, according to Chinese state media, adding: "If mishandled, the two nations could collide or even come into conflict."

Asked if he foresaw a conflict with China over Taiwan, Trump had said: "No, I don't think so. I think we'll be fine. [Xi] doesn't want to see a war."

China has ramped up military drills around the island in recent years, raising tensions in the region and testing the balance that Washington has struck.

Late last year, the Trump administration announced an $11bn ($8bn) package of weapons to be sold to Taiwan , including advanced rocket launchers and a variety of missiles, which Beijing condemned.

Trump said he would soon decide whether that sale could go ahead, adding that he and Xi had discussed it "in great detail".

title.en: Donald Trump does ‘not feel optimistic’ for Jimmy Lai after speaking with Xi Jinping
title.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普与习近平通话后对黎智英的命运“不感乐观”

summary.en: US President Donald Trump raised the case of jailed Hong Kong democracy campaigner Jimmy Lai during talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, but was reportedly told it was a "tough" issue, leading Trump to express a lack of optimism for Lai's release.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在与中国领导人习近平的会谈中提及了被囚禁的香港民主倡导者黎智英的案件，但据报道被告知这是一个“棘手”的问题，导致特朗普对黎智英的获释表示不乐观。

body.en:
Donald Trump raised the case of jailed Hong Kong democracy campaigner Jimmy Lai in talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping but was told it “is a tough one”.

Family and supporters of the 78-year-old British citizen had hoped the US president could help secure his release.

Lai was sentenced to 20 years in prison in February under a security law imposed by Beijing.

The media tycoon, who was an influential figure in the former British territory’s pro-democracy movement , was arrested in 2020 in a crackdown after massive anti-government protests.

Lai’s legal team says he has health problems , fuelling fears he may die behind bars.

Speaking onboard Air Force One as he returned from his two-day visit to China , Trump said he believed Xi was seriously considering freeing a church pastor detained in China, but was less hopeful over the plight of Lai.

Trump said: “I did bring it up, but it’s a tougher one for him. He said Jimmy Lai is a ‘tough one’ for him.”

In an interview with Fox News broadcast later, Trump said: “I bought up Jimmy Lai. I would say the response to that was not positive.”

Lai’s daughter Claire said she was grateful to Trump for his commitment to her father’s release.

She said: “He has earned his reputation as liberating the unjustly detained and I am confident he and his administration will be the ones to free my father.”

She added it was an opportunity for Xi to do “the only just and honourable thing”.

Lai, a diabetic, has been kept in solitary confinement without air conditioning in a jail where summer temperatures rise to 44C (111F), his children have said.

“He has lost a very significant amount of weight, visibly, and he is a lot weaker than he was before,” Claire said in remarks to media earlier this year.

“His nails turn almost purple, gray and greenish before they fall off, and his teeth are getting rotten.”

At the end of last year, Trump told reporters he had spoken to Xi about releasing Lai .

“I feel so badly. I spoke to President Xi about it, and I asked to consider his release,” Trump said, without specifying the date he had asked Xi. “He’s an older man and he’s not well. So I did put that request out. We’ll see what happens.”

Lai’s case has sparked international concern, particularly in the UK, where he is seen as being punished for defending democratic undertakings given in 1997 with the handover of Hong Kong from British to Chinese rule.
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普在与中国领导人习近平的会谈中提出了被监禁的香港民主运动人士黎智英的案件，但被告知这是“一个艰难的案件”。 这位 78 岁英国公民的家人和支持者曾希望美国总统能够帮助他获释。 黎智英今年 2 月根据北京实施的国安法被判处 20 年徒刑。 这位媒体大亨是前英国领土民主运动中的一位有影响力的人物，他于 2020 年大规模反政府抗议活动后的一次镇压中被捕。 黎智英的法律团队表示，他有健康问题，这加剧了人们对他可能死于狱中的担忧。 特朗普结束对中国为期两天的访问，在空军一号上发表讲话时表示，他相信习近平正在认真考虑释放一名在中国被拘留的教会牧师，但对黎智英的困境不太抱有希望。 特朗普说：“我确实提出过，但这对他来说是一个更艰难的问题。他说黎智英对他来说是一个‘难缠的人’。” 在随后播出的福克斯新闻采访中，特朗普表示：“我收购了黎智英。我想说，对此的反应并不积极。” 赖的女儿克莱尔表示，她感谢特朗普对她父亲获释的承诺。 她说：“他因解放被不公正拘留的人而赢得了声誉，我相信他和他的政府将释放我的父亲。” 她补充说，这是习近平做“唯一公正和光荣的事情”的机会。 黎是一名糖尿病患者，他的孩子们说，他被单独监禁在没有空调的监狱里，那里夏季气温高达 44 摄氏度（111 华氏度）。 “他的体重明显减轻了很多，而且比以前虚弱了很多，”克莱尔今年早些时候在接受媒体采访时说道。 “他的指甲在脱落之前几乎变成紫色、灰色和绿色，他的牙齿也开始腐烂。” 去年年底，特朗普告诉记者，他已与习近平谈过释放黎智英的事宜。 “我感觉很糟糕。我和习主席谈过这件事，我要求考虑释放他，”特朗普说，但没有具体说明他向习主席询问的日期。 “他年纪大了，身体不太好。所以我确实提出了这个请求。我们会看看会发生什么。” 黎智英的案件引发了国际社会的关注，特别是在英国，他被认为是因为捍卫 1997 年香港从英国移交到中国统治期间做出的民主承诺而受到惩罚。

title.en: As Xi sets a new power dynamic, Trump leaves China with little to brag about
title.zh: 习近平确立新权力格局，特朗普对中国无甚可夸耀

summary.en: A recent summit between the leaders of China and the United States, while largely cordial, indicated a potential shift in the balance of power between the two nations.
summary.zh: 在中美两国领导人的一次大致友好的峰会期间，有迹象表明两国之间的权力平衡可能正在发生变化。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump hailed it as “the biggest summit ever.” In reality, his less than 48 lavish hours in China yielded few results.

Expectations for any real breakthroughs were always low. But what we saw at the high-stakes summit could still shape the US-China relationship for months and years to come.

China had been signalling for weeks that Taiwan would be its top priority at this summit.

The island’s status has always been a point of conflict between the US and Chinese governments; China claims it as a self-governing province that will eventually be brought under its control, while the US has long been its single largest supplier of the weapons needed to prevent that from happening.

But this week, Chinese President Xi Jinping took it one step further; saying explicitly that from now on, the most important factor in the US-China relationship would be how the US deals with Taiwan.

“The Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations,” Xi told Trump, according to the Chinese Foreign Ministry handout. “If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability. If handled poorly, the two countries will collide or even clash, putting the entire US-China relationship in an extremely dangerous situation.”

When asked for his version of events later in the day, Trump opted to say nothing. His silence was seen as a win in Taiwan, where fears he might go off script and say something to inadvertently shift the US’ position on the island were high going into the summit.

“US policy on the issue of Taiwan is unchanged as of today and as of the meeting that we had here today,” US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said. “It was raised. They always raised it on their side. We always make clear our position and we move on to other topics.”

But China has made its position clear; the US’ ongoing support for Taiwan could jeopardise one of its most important trade relationships.

The US approved a US$15b ($2.09b) arms package for Taiwan in December last year; its largest ever. But with Trump still yet to give his final approval, its delivery had been stalled.

Whether or not those weapons finally reach Taiwan may be the first real test of whether Xi’s threat made an impact.

While the summit was largely cordial, there were moments that signalled the balance of power between the two leaders might be shifting.

Xi rolled out the red carpet and did a lot to make Trump feel respected; sending his Vice President to greet him at the airport, personally accompanying him on a tour of the Temple of Heaven, and allowing him to visit the highly secretive Zhongnanhai compound, where he and other senior Chinese Communist...
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普称赞这是“有史以来规模最大的峰会”。事实上，他在中国度过的不到48个小时的奢华时光并没有取得什么成果。 对任何真正突破的期望总是很低。但我们在这次高风险峰会上看到的情况仍可能影响未来数月乃至数年的美中关系。 几周来，中国一直在暗示台湾将是此次峰会的首要任务。 该岛的地位一直是美国和中国政府之间的冲突点。中国声称它是一个自治省，最终将受到其控制，而美国长期以来一直是其最大的武器供应商，以防止这种情况发生。 但本周，中国国家主席习近平更进一步；明确表示，今后美中关系最重要的因素将是美国如何对待台湾。 根据中国外交部的讲义，习近平对特朗普说：“台湾问题是中美关系中最重要的问题。” “如果处理得当，双边关系将保持总体稳定。如果处理不好，两国就会发生冲突甚至冲突，使整个美中关系处于极其危险的境地。” 当天晚些时候，当被问及他对事件的看法时，特朗普选择什么也不说。他的沉默在台湾被视为一种胜利，在峰会上，人们非常担心他可能会脱离剧本，说出一些无意中改变美国在台湾的立场的话。 美国国务卿卢比奥表示：“截至今天以及我们今天在这里举行的会议，美国在台湾问题上的政策没有变化。” “有人提出了。他们总是站在自己一边提出。我们总是明确我们的立场，然后转向其他话题。” 但中方已经明确表明立场，美国对台湾的持续支持可能会危及其最重要的贸易关系之一。 去年 12 月，美国批准了一项价值 150 亿美元（2.09b 美元）的台湾军售计划；其规模有史以来最大。但由于特朗普尚未给予最终批准，其交付已陷入停滞。 这些武器最终是否到达台湾可能是习近平的威胁是否产生影响的第一个真正考验。 尽管这次峰会基本上是友好的，但有些时刻表明两位领导人之间的权力平衡可能正在发生变化。 习近平铺上红地毯，做了很多让特朗普感到受到尊重的事情；派副总统到机场迎接他，亲自陪同他游览天坛，并允许他参观高度保密的中南海大院，他和其他中共高级官员都在那里……

reflection.en: News of shifting power dynamics between nations reminds us that human authority is ultimately transient. Psalm 75:7 offers a profound perspective, reminding us that it is God who judges, lifting up one and bringing down another. This truth invites us to look beyond temporary political tides and trust in a higher, unchanging sovereignty.
reflection.zh: 国家间权力动态的变化提醒我们，人类的权威终究是暂时的。诗篇75:7提供了一个深刻的视角，提醒我们是雅伟施行审判，他使这人降卑，使那人升高。这一真理邀请我们超越暂时的政治潮流，信靠那至高无上、永不改变的主权。

verse.textEn: It is God who judges: He brings one down, he exalts another.
verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

title.en: What China critics in Maga movement make of Trump's Beijing trip
title.zh: MAGA运动中的中国批评者如何看待特朗普的北京之行

summary.en: Trump’s shift to a more conciliatory stance on China is expected by experts to influence the broader MAGA movement, potentially leading to a similar softening of views among his supporters.
summary.zh: 专家表示，特朗普对中国采取的更温和态度，可能会影响到更广泛的MAGA支持者群体。

body.en:
When Donald Trump strode on to a stage at a campaign rally in Indiana in 2016, he made one thing clear: China was America's chief economic antagonist.

"We can't continue to allow China to rape our country," he told a crowd in Fort Wayne. "We have the cards. Don't forget it."

The anti-China rhetoric didn't let up - through a decade of rallies, his 2024 campaign and into his second term.

Trump arrived back at the White House alongside key allies who made China-bashing a calling card: Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Vice-President JD Vance and senior economic counsellor Peter Navarro - all united in accusing Beijing of "ripping off" America, stealing technology at an industrial scale and flooding US streets with fentanyl.

Tariffs soon followed, climbing from 10% in February 2025 to 145% by mid-April's "Liberation Day", as Trump called his launch of import taxes on China and scores of other US trade partners. China struck back, slapping the US with 125% tariffs and blocking rare earth exports. A trade war was under way.

Trump stepped on to a red carpet at the Great Hall of the People to hundreds of flag-waving children and a military band belting out the Star-Spangled Banner.

"It's an honour to be with you," Trump told Chinese President Xi Jinping. "It's an honour to be your friend, and the relationship between China and the US is going to be better than ever before."

Trump soon hailed "fantastic trade deals", although no major breakthrough was confirmed. Chipmaker Nvidia was reportedly given a go-ahead to sell semiconductors to 10 Chinese companies and Boeing secured an order for 200 aircraft. Citi was granted an approval to operate a securities business in China.

But amid the pleasantries and softened positions, hardline positions against China reflect the traditionally more hawkish stance of Trump's Republican Party.

Less than a week before the summit, the US state department sanctioned three Chinese firms for providing satellite imagery to Iran to help strike US forces in the Middle East.

And outstanding issues remain - chiefly Taiwan, the self-ruled island viewed by Beijing as a renegade province. Trump delivered few details on the fate of a delayed $14bn arms sale viewed as essential by Democrats and Republican China "hawks" alike.

Ahead of the visit, a bipartisan group of senators sent a letter urging Trump to move ahead with the sale and "formally" notify his Chinese counterpart.

"On Taiwan, he [Xi] feels very strongly. I made no commitment either way," Trump told reporters on Air Force One, adding that he would make a "determination over the next fairly short period" about the arms sale.

body.zh: 2016 年，当唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 登上印第安纳州竞选集会的讲台时，他明确表示了一件事：中国是美国的主要经济对手。 “我们不能继续允许中国强奸我们的国家，”他在韦恩堡对人群说。 “我们有牌。别忘了。” 从十年的集会、2024 年的竞选活动到第二个任期，反华言论并未减弱。 特朗普回到白宫时，与以抨击中国为名片的主要盟友一起回到白宫：国务卿马可·鲁比奥、副总统万斯和高级经济顾问彼得·纳瓦罗，他们一致指责北京“敲诈”美国，大规模窃取技术，并让芬太尼充斥美国街头。 关税紧随其后，从 2025 年 2 月的 10% 攀升至 4 月中旬的“解放日”，特朗普称其对中国和其他数十个美国贸易伙伴征收进口税。中国予以反击，向美国征收 125% 的关税，并阻止稀土出口。一场贸易战正在进行中。 特朗普走上人民大会堂的红地毯，数百名挥舞旗帜的儿童和军乐队高奏星条旗。 特朗普对中国国家主席习近平说：“很荣幸与你们在一起。” “很荣幸成为你的朋友，中美关系将比以往任何时候都更好。” 特朗普很快就称赞了“出色的贸易协议”，尽管没有确认重大突破。据报道，芯片制造商英伟达已获准向 10 家中国公司出售半导体，而波音公司则获得了 200 架飞机的订单。花旗获准在中国经营证券业务。 但在寒暄和软化立场中，针对中国的强硬立场反映了特朗普领导的共和党传统上更为强硬的立场。 峰会前不到一周，美国国务院制裁了三家中国公司，因为它们向伊朗提供卫星图像，以帮助打击驻中东的美军。 悬而未决的问题依然存在——主要是台湾，这个被北京视为叛逆省份的自治岛屿。特朗普没有透露有关延迟的 140 亿美元军售的细节，民主党和共和党的对华“鹰派”都认为这很重要。 在访问之前，一个由两党参议员组成的小组致函敦促特朗普推进出售事宜，并“正式”通知中国同行。 特朗普在空军一号上对记者说：“在台湾问题上，他（习近平）的感受非常强烈。无论如何，我都没有做出任何承诺。”他补充说，他将“在接下来相当短的时间内”就军售问题做出决定。 值得注意的是，中国对这次会议的宣读将台湾作为中心议题，认为未能解决这一问题可能会导致“冲突和……”

reflection.en: Leaders often set the tone and direction for those who follow them, shaping collective perspectives and approaches. This story reminds us that where there is a lack of clear guidance, people may falter, but wise counsel can provide stability and a path forward.

title.en: Pakistan faces pressure over mediator role in Iran war
title.zh: 巴基斯坦在伊朗战争调解中面临压力

summary.en: Pakistan is navigating a complex geopolitical landscape as it attempts to mediate in a major conflict involving Iran, balancing relationships with Washington, Tehran, Beijing, and key Gulf allies. Recent media scrutiny has intensified the pressure on Islamabad.
summary.zh: 巴基斯坦正努力调解一场涉及伊朗的重大地缘政治冲突，同时需平衡与华盛顿、德黑兰、北京以及主要海湾盟友的关系，这使其面临复杂的局面。近期一份美国媒体报道进一步加剧了伊斯兰堡所承受的压力。

body.en:
With Pakistan stepping in the middle of a major geopolitical conflict, Islamabad is forced to balance between Washington, Tehran, Beijing and key Gulf allies. A recent US media report places it under even more scrutiny.

Pakistan has taken on a leading role in the peace efforts between the US and Iran , hosting talks and serving as an intermediary for backchannel diplomacy between the warring parties .

For Islamabad, the stakes are high. Officials view stability in the Gulf as closely tied to the country's own economic and security interests. A broader confrontation between the US and Iran could disrupt trade routes, deepen energy pressures, inflame sectarian tensions and further destabilize Pakistan's sensitive border regions with Iran.

International prestige is also at play for the Pakistani government as they work to end a conflict affecting the entire world . But this also means a risk of reputational damage.

"Pakistan risks growing criticism if its efforts to revive US-Iran talks fail, especially after publicly taking a leading mediation role," Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow for South Asia at the Washington-based Atlantic Council, told DW. 

"With talks stalled, Pakistan's options are limited because a mediator cannot force two deeply distrustful sides to negotiate," he added.

"Pakistan is trying its best to engage both parties and views the escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran with grave concern," a senior government official involved in the negotiation process told DW. 

"We are committed to playing a constructive diplomatic role to support immediate de-escalation and a peaceful resolution in the interest of regional and global security," the official added. 

Earlier this week, a report in US media raised doubt over Pakistan's neutrality in the Iran conflict. Citing unnamed US officials, CBS News reported that Pakistan had allowed Iran to park its aircraft on Pakistani airbases , effectively shielding them from US strikes.

Pakistan's Foreign Office immediately responded by calling the report "misleading" and "speculative." In an official statement, Islamabad said the aircraft activity was linked to diplomatic and logistical arrangements connected to ongoing peace efforts and involved personnel from multiple sides.

The Foreign Office also warned that "unverified and sensationalized reporting" risked undermining sensitive diplomatic initiatives.

US Senator Lindsey Graham, an outspoken supporter of the US war in Iran, publicly criticized Pakistan following the CBS report. His remarks reflect broader concerns among some US policymakers who fear Pakistan may be appearing too accommodating toward Tehran while still seeking to preserve strategic ties with Washington.

body.zh: 随着巴基斯坦陷入重大地缘政治冲突，伊斯兰堡被迫在华盛顿、德黑兰、北京和主要海湾盟友之间保持平衡。美国媒体最近的一篇报道对其进行了更严格的审查。 巴基斯坦在美国和伊朗之间的和平努力中发挥了主导作用，主办了会谈并充当交战双方之间秘密外交的调解人。 对于伊斯兰堡来说，风险很高。官员们认为海湾地区的稳定与该国自身的经济和安全利益密切相关。美国和伊朗之间更广泛的对抗可能会扰乱贸易路线，加深能源压力，加剧宗派紧张局势，并进一步破坏巴基斯坦与伊朗敏感边境地区的稳定。 巴基斯坦政府在努力结束影响全世界的冲突时，国际声誉也发挥着重要作用。但这也意味着声誉受损的风险。 华盛顿大西洋理事会南亚高级研究员迈克尔·库格曼（Michael Kugelman）告诉德国之声：“如果巴基斯坦恢复美伊谈判的努力失败，特别是在公开发挥主导调解作用之后，巴基斯坦将面临越来越多的批评。” 他补充说：“随着谈判陷入僵局，巴基斯坦的选择受到限制，因为调解人无法迫使两个极度不信任的双方进行谈判。” 一位参与谈判进程的高级政府官员告诉德国之声：“巴基斯坦正在尽最大努力与双方接触，并对华盛顿和德黑兰之间不断升级的紧张局势表示严重关切。” 这位官员补充道：“我们致力于发挥建设性的外交作用，支持立即缓和局势并和平解决问题，以维护地区和全球安全。” 本周早些时候，美国媒体的一篇报道对巴基斯坦在伊朗冲突中的中立性提出了质疑。哥伦比亚广播公司新闻援引未透露姓名的美国官员的话说，巴基斯坦允许伊朗将其飞机停放在巴基斯坦空军基地，从而有效地保护它们免受美国的袭击。 巴基斯坦外交部立即回应称该报告“具有误导性”和“推测性”。伊斯兰堡在一份官方声明中表示，飞机活动与正在进行的和平努力相关的外交和后勤安排有关，涉及多方人员。 英国外交部还警告说，“未经证实和耸人听闻的报道”可能会破坏敏感的外交举措。 美国参议员林赛·格雷厄姆是美国对伊朗战争的直言不讳的支持者，在哥伦比亚广播公司的报道后公开批评巴基斯坦。他的言论反映了一些美国政策制定者更广泛的担忧，他们担心巴基斯坦可能对德黑兰过于宽容，同时仍寻求维持与华盛顿的战略关系。 与此同时，美国...

reflection.en: Pakistan's challenging role as a mediator highlights the immense difficulty and pressure involved in seeking peace between powerful nations. Even amidst such complex geopolitical balancing acts, the pursuit of reconciliation remains a profound and blessed endeavor.
reflection.zh: 巴基斯坦作为调解者的艰难角色，凸显了在强国之间寻求和平所涉及的巨大困难和压力。即使在如此复杂的地缘政治平衡中，追求和解仍然是一项深刻而蒙福的事业。

summary.en: Donald Trump's visit to Beijing concluded with his goal of securing China's help to end the war in Iran appearing uncertain. During the summit, Chinese President Xi Jinping also used the opportunity to issue a warning to the US regarding Taiwan.

body.en:
Donald Trump hopes to have China help him end the war in Iran, but this goal seemed far from guaranteed as he wrapped up his two-day visit to Beijing. Xi Jinping, in turn, took the chance to warn the US over Taiwan.

The high-profile Beijing summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping ended with bombastic, positive statements — especially from the Trump White House, which called the US president "the dealmaker-in-chief" — but with little info known about concrete deals between the two rival superpowers.

Trump praised Xi during the visit, calling him a "great leader" and "a man I respect greatly."

Addressing reporters at a press event alongside Xi, Trump also indicated that he and Xi "feel very similar" about the Iran war, which has been dominating global politics since the US and Israel launched air strikes on Iran in late February .

"We want that to end. We don't want them to have a nuclear weapon. We want the straits open," Trump said.  

This echoed Trump's previous claims of Xi offering to help broker a deal with Tehran and open the Strait of Hormuz .

The Chinese leader, however, did not mention Iran in his remarks to the press on Friday. Instead, Xi took the chance to warn of a potential conflict between China and the US if the two nations fail to cooperate. He highlighted the dispute over Taiwan , the self-ruled island which China sees as its own territory.

"The Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations,"  Xi said.

"If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability. Otherwise, the two countries will have clashes and even conflicts, putting the entire relationship in great jeopardy."

With global economy in turmoil over the Strait of Hormuz, neither side seems willing to return to the bruising trade war of 2025 .

The US president was accompanied by more than a dozen CEOs, including Nvidia's Jensen Huang, Apple's Tim Cook and Tesla's Elon Musk .

On Friday, Trump touted "fantastic trade deals for both countries," without providing details.

Joseph Bosco, a former China Country Desk Officer in the US Office of the Secretary of Defense, told DW that Xi was trying to "exploit Trump's obvious vulnerabilities at this point."

Trump "has the Iran war going on, which is not going according to his original plan. And I think Xi Jinping thought this is a good time to press very hard on the most important issue that they perceive, which is Taiwan," Bosco said.

Taiwanese authorities fear Beijing taking over the island by force , and rely heavily on US arms sales to maintain its defense capabilities.
